overview: The Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme (ECHS) is a cashless and capless health scheme launched on April 1, 2003, by the Ministry of Defence to provide comprehensive medical facilities to retired armed forces personnel and their dependents. It operates through a network of ECHS Polyclinics and empanelled civil hospitals, offering indoor/outdoor treatment, tests, and medicines without monetary ceiling on treatment. The scheme is financed by the Government of India and aims to deliver quality healthcare by leveraging existing Armed Forces infrastructure and empanelling civil healthcare providers.
objectives: Provide quality medicare to retirees of the Armed Forces
Manage the scheme through existing Armed Forces infrastructure to minimise administrative expenditure
Ensure minimal disruption of the Scheme during war/training and availability of ECHS services in non-military areas
Empanel civil hospitals and diagnostic centres to expand healthcare access
Provide life-time contribution-based membership with no age or medical condition bar
Offer reimbursement at CGHS rates for emergency treatment in non-empanelled facilities
Cover spouse and all eligible dependents of ECHS members
Ensure no monetary ceiling on treatment for beneficiaries
eligibility: Retired Armed Forces personnel till 2002 could avail medical facilities only for specific high cost surgery/treatment for a limited number of diseases covered under the Army Group Insurance(Medical Branch Scheme) (AGI(MBS)) and Armed Forces Group Insurance Scheme(Management Information System) (AFGIS (MIS)) schemes. Based on the noble aim of establishing a medicare system for retirees, ECHS was authorised vide Government of India, Ministry of Defence letter No 22(i) 01/US/D(Res) dated 30 Dec 2002 and launched with effect from 01 Apr 2003. Ex-servicemen pensioners and their dependants who were only entitled for treatment in service hospital are now authorised treatment in service hospitals and in civil/private hospitals specifically empanelled with the ECHS.
benefits: No age or medical condition bar for becoming a member. Life time contribution ranges from Rs 30,000/- to Rs 1,20,000/- (depending upon Grade Pay). Provision for re-imbursement at CGHS rates in case of treatment under Emergency in a non-empanelled facility. No monetary ceiling on treatment. Indoor/outdoor treatment, tests and medicines. Familiar environment and sense of belongingness. Covers spouse and all eligible dependents.
financial_support: The Scheme is financed by Govt of India. The existing infrastructure includes command and control structure, spare capacity of Service Medical facilities (Hospitals and MI Rooms), procurement organisations for medical and non medical equipment, defence land and buildings etc. In order to ensure minimal disruption of the Scheme during war/training and availability of ECHS services in non military areas, resources are supplemented by establishing new Armed Forces Polyclinics in Non Military areas, augmenting existing medical facilities/clinics in selected military stations, empanelling civil hospitals and diagnostic centres, and providing finances.
application_process: 1. Retired Armed Forces personnel and their dependents become eligible for ECHS membership upon retirement. 2. Members must make a one-time contribution based on their Grade Pay at the time of retirement, ranging from Rs 30,000/- to Rs 1,20,000/-. 3. Upon payment, members receive an ECHS card enabling access to empanelled facilities. 4. For treatment, beneficiaries visit ECHS Polyclinics or empanelled hospitals. 5. In emergencies, treatment can be sought at non-empanelled facilities with reimbursement at CGHS rates. 6. Annual validation of dependents above 18 years is required (excluding spouse) as per CO ECHS letter No B/49711-NSC/AG/ECHS/Gen Corrs dt 10 Jun 25. 7. Beneficiaries must carry out Annual Validation as per directives; in case of issues, contact jditechs1[at]echs[dot]gov[dot]in. 8. For card-related issues, email echs-card[at]echs[dot]gov[dot]in or call Toll Free No: 1800 114 115. 9. For general issues, contact via echs[at]sourceinfosys[dot]com or WhatsApp on +91-7703818578 / 7701976194 / 8448086480 / 8448086481.
required_documents: Proof of retirement from Armed Forces
Grade Pay details for contribution calculation
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Defence, Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare (DoESW)
contact_details: Email: echs[at]sourceinfosys[dot]com | WhatsApp: +91-7703818578 / 7701976194 / 8448086480 / 8448086481 | Toll Free No: 1800 114 115 | Card-related issues: echs-card[at]echs[dot]gov[dot]in | Annual validation queries: jditechs1[at]echs[dot]gov[dot]in
caveats: Beneficiaries can avail medical facility from only one Govt Agency; temporary exit from ECHS requires blocking of 64 KB ECHS Card for safe custody when availing facility from Central/State Govt or Public Sector undertaking.
Online Temporary Slips get blocked after 90 days from OTP generation if 64 KB ECHS Cards are not collected.
Annual Validation is required for all dependents above 18 years (excluding spouse); failure to comply may affect benefits.
Treatment in non-empanelled facilities is reimbursable only at CGHS rates and requires emergency justification.
NABH accredited medical facilities are empanelled only for the validity of NABH certificate; MoA renewed upon revalidation/renewal of NABH certificate.
Certain investigations or prosthetic fitments taking longer than 60 days may incur a 30% deduction unless waiver is obtained.
Total monthly cap for NA medicine bills is Rs 25,000/- under one claim ID; fresh timeline for submission of Hard Copy or Online claims is within 60 days of medicine bills date.
ECHS beneficiaries above 80 years of age are exempted from annual validation for 64KB ECHS Smart Card holders.
Printing of 64KB ECHS Smart Cards may be temporarily stopped due to vendor delays; validity of temporary slips extended accordingly.
